text:
Julie (AE): @here quick sync — FinReg (EU) is asking for a PoC next sprint. Requirements: EU + APAC regional routing, explicit list of subprocessors, where TLS terminates, and a basic dedicated-capacity price for a 2-week trial. Can eng/security confirm feasibility and what we can hand over to procurement?

Raj S: They expect ~50 qps peak, avg 2k tokens/req. Target p99 latency <200ms EU. They also asked if we can guarantee no cross-region replication for logs/backups during the POC.

Alex W: Short answer: yes for the POC if we do Dedicated or Private. Hosted multi-tenant EU region gives residency (data stored in eu region) but not the same isolation guarantees as Dedicated/Private.

Alex W: For hosted: we have regional endpoints (e.g. api.eu.redwood.ai) — traffic terminates at our regional LB and then goes to GPUs in that region. TLS is terminated at the edge LB (we manage certs). For Private we can support customer-managed certs and customer-controlled termination.

Maria D: Subprocessor list (high level) we can provide for the security questionnaire: AWS (eu-west-1), GCP (europe-west3 / asia-east1 for APAC fallbacks), Azure (w europe), Cloudflare (edge routing), Datadog (metrics), S3-compatible object storage (backups). For the PoC we can scope to only eu/asia zones and exclude cross-region backups if they require. :lock:

Samir K: Recommend Dedicated pool scoped to eu-west1 for 2 GPUs equivalent (handles their QPS + KV cache). Quick ballpark for a short PoC (2 weeks with reserved burst): ~$6k-$10k depending on instance class and tokens. If they want private deployment (on-prem/VPC) add setup fee (~$4k-8k) and a 1-week provisioning lead time. These are draft numbers — finance to confirm.

Julie (AE): Maria — can we provide the subprocessors as a one-pager (csv + contact email) and a cert chain dump? Procurement asked for cert chain and TLS termination diagram.

Maria D: Yes. I can produce: 1) subprocessors CSV, 2) cert chain PEM files (leaf + intermediates) + CA fingerprints, 3) short diagram showing where TLS terminates for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Need to know whether they want MIL-STD level of detail or just procurement-level.

Julie (AE): Procurement wants cert chain + attestation and confirmation that logs/backups for the PoC will remain in-region. They asked about CDN/edge vendors — will they see plaintext?

Alex W: For Hosted: TLS terminates at our regional load balancer (we do TLS offload), then internal traffic is mTLS within our VPC clusters. Edge vendors (Cloudflare) do not see plaintext unless we explicitly enable their TLS termination (we usually keep edge TLS->origin TLS). For Private we can place the LB inside the customer VPC and maintain customer-managed TLS.

Samir K: On the replication question: we can disable cross-region backups and keep logs in-region for the PoC window. Need to add S3 bucket policy + retention config. I’ll prepare the CLI snippet for the Ops runbook.

Samir K: CLI snippet for routing header we can ask the app to include if they want explicit region pinning:```json
{
  "x-redwood-region": "eu",
  "prefer-local": true
}```This is read by the gateway and used as a routing hint — not a hard enforcement unless on Dedicated/Private.

Raj S: Action items: (1) Maria: subprocessors CSV + cert chain + diagram (2) Alex/Samir: short tech one-pager explaining termination + routing behavior + ops snippet (3) Julie: finalize PoC SOW and numbers for procurement. Timeline: PoC kickoff in 10 business days if provisioning ok.

Maria D: I’ll produce the docs and attach the PEMs + a short SOC2/Security cover note. ETA 48h.

Alex W: I’ll scope the Dedicated footprint and confirm GPU type + exact latency numbers. Can we get expected token distribution per request? That changes cache sizing.

Julie (AE): I’ll ask the customer for token distribution and whether they want private VPC. Thanks team — I’ll collate and share with procurement. :thumbsup:
